archetype.name: Bubble Team (goaltending-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose goalies and shot suppression keep it in nearly every game while a low-volume attack and weak power play keep it from pulling away, which leaves it hovering around the Metropolitan's playoff line.

report.headline: Elite goaltending again masks an attack that can't generate enough
report.take:
Eight games in, the Islanders look like the Islanders. They sit 4-3-1, fourth in the Metropolitan, and 12th on the site, and the formula matches recent years: keep shots to the outside, let the goalie win the night, and hope the offense finds three. Ilya Sorokin is stopping .940 with 8.0 goals saved above expected in six starts, the team's Goalies GSAx of 10.4 leads the league, and only one team allows fewer shots on goal than their 20.8 a game. That is why goals allowed per game rank fourth. It is not new either. Last season's goalies saved 40.1 above expected and the defense ranked fifth, and in 2022-23 it was 41.1.

The record and the goal differential tell different stories, and the honest read is in between. A +6 differential should be worth more than nine points, and the Pts vs Goal Diff of -2.2 ranks 30th, so close games have broken against them. The two one-goal losses and the overtime loss in Ottawa show it. But the differential is itself inflated. The 5-on-5 PDO is 104.6, the all-situations figure of 106 is third in the league, and the skaters are shooting .121 against a league .113. Underneath, the xGF % of 48.6 ranks 21st. They hold the puck about evenly (CF % 51.0) but give up the better chances. Take away the hot goaltending and this is a team that loses the expected-goals battle by a little.

The attack is the chronic problem. Shots on goal come in at 24.9 a game, 2.3 below the league, and the offense ranks 19th. Offense rank has sat between 22nd and 28th in each of the last five seasons. The power play is at 16.7%, 23rd, after 15.8%, 20.3%, 12.6% and 16.5% in prior years, so that is a trait, not a slump. Bo Horvat (9 points, ninth among 220 centers) and Matthew Schaefer (7 assists in 25.8 minutes a night) carry most of the production. The blueline grades D+ because the minutes behind Schaefer, Pelech and especially Pulock, who ranks 212th of 242, are not giving much back.

The pace of 92 points almost exactly repeats last year's 91, and that feels like the right neighborhood. Sorokin will not stay at .940, but the Islanders have a track record of goaltending well above average, and some of the close-game bad luck should flip. The two forces roughly cancel. Unless the offense finds another gear, this is a bubble team for the fourth time in five years.

strengths.title: Sorokin and a league-best GSAx
strengths.body: The goalies have saved 10.4 goals above expected, first in the league, and Sorokin ranks second among 65 goalies on the tab. The .940 will come down. Still, this franchise posted 41.1 and 40.1 GSAx in two of the last four seasons, so elite goaltending is the baseline here rather than a fluke. Expect a regression to very good, not to average.

strengths.title: Shot suppression and a sharp PK
strengths.body: Opponents get only 20.8 shots on goal a game, second fewest, and the penalty kill runs at 86.7%, sixth. Forwards against them are being held well under their usual output, third best in the league. That combination is structural and should hold better than the save percentage.

strengths.title: Horvat driving the top of the lineup
strengths.body: Horvat has 5 goals and 9 points with 4 on the power play, ninth among centers, while logging 20.6 minutes. Maccelli and Palat, whose 68.1% xGF is the best on the roster, give the middle six some real play-driving. The depth scoring is thin, so the burden on Horvat is heavy.

concerns.title: Out-chanced once the goalie is removed
concerns.body: A 48.6 xGF % ranks 21st, so the +6 differential rests on a 104.6 PDO and above-league shooting. Even possession (51.0 CF %) is not turning into better looks. When Sorokin cools, the margins of these games will shrink.

concerns.title: Low shot volume, weak power play
concerns.body: They put 24.9 shots on goal a game, 24th in the league. The power play converts 16.7% against a league 20.4%. Both are multi-year traits: the offense has ranked 22nd or worse in each of the last five seasons. This is the ceiling on the whole team.

concerns.title: Thin blueline behind Schaefer
concerns.body: The defense grades D+. Pulock has no points and ranks 212th of 242 in nearly 19 minutes a night, and Pelech ranks 176th. Opposing defensemen are out-producing their norms (24th) and taking an outsized share of the points allowed, a sign the back end gets caught on the rush.

trend.note: They have alternated results all season, with no streak longer than one game either way. The last five (3-1-1, a .700 points %) are a slight step up but play almost identically to the season.

weekAhead.headline: Leaky Kings at home, then Dallas's mirror-image goaltending wall
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with two home games against teams ranked 19th and 31st on the site. Anaheim is a middling 4-3-0 team with a dangerous power play (26.9%) and a below-average save percentage. Los Angeles is 0-4-2 with F grades in goal and on defense and a 61.9% penalty kill, though its 50.8 xGF % and 29.8 shots a game say it is better than the record. Banking points at home here matters, because the road half is harder.

Dallas is essentially the Islanders in a mirror: first in goals against, a .944 save percentage, a league-leading hold on opposing forwards, and a bottom-six offense. Expect a low-event game decided by a goal. Nashville is the softer road stop at 5-on-5 (44.0 CF %, 27th), but its 29.6% power play makes discipline the key. Three or more wins from four is realistic; anything less likely means the attack went cold against Dallas.

keyMatchups.title: Power play versus LA's broken kill
keyMatchups.body: The Islanders' 16.7% power play is a season-long weakness. Los Angeles kills only 61.9%, 31st, behind a .861 team save percentage. If the unit can't cash in this week, that says more about the unit than about bad luck.

keyMatchups.title: Goals at a premium in Dallas
keyMatchups.body: Dallas ranks first in goals against and has held opposing forwards furthest under their norms, first in the league. With the Islanders' own low shot volume, expect very few chances. Sorokin against an A+ goaltending group probably decides it.

keyMatchups.title: Staying out of the box
keyMatchups.body: Anaheim (26.9%) and Nashville (29.6%) both run top-six power plays. The Islanders' 86.7% kill is good enough to blunt them, but against teams this limited at 5-on-5, special teams are their best path to scoring.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the power play finally converts against Los Angeles's 61.9% kill. If it can't there, it won't anywhere.

restOfSeason.body:
Two sustainable pieces hold this team up: shot suppression, and goaltending that has been well above average in most recent seasons. The piece that will fade is the 104.6 PDO. Sorokin's .940 and above-league team shooting will drift down, and a 48.6 xGF % says the even-strength game is slightly losing. Working the other way, the -2.2 Pts vs Goal Diff is mostly bad luck in close games and should even out, so the standings may hold steady even as the margins shrink.

The result is a team that projects much like last season's 91-point club: in the race for a wild card or a third Metropolitan spot, but not a contender. The swing factor is offense. Five straight seasons of bottom-third scoring argue against a breakout, but a power play even at league average would push them toward the top of the range.
swingFactors: How far Sorokin's save % falls from .940
A power play that reaches league average

confidence.note: Only eight games and a PDO-heavy start, but the profile matches several seasons of history.
